new_candidates.body:
### Summary

`ReplayBuffer.from_lerobot_dataset()` stores video-backed camera frames as **float32 in [0, 255]** instead of [0, 1]. With the default `OnlineOfflineMixer` (50/50), half of every training batch then has image inputs roughly 255× larger than the online half. The same values also make every checkpoint dump fail: each PNG write is rejected, and `save_episode()` then raises `FileNotFoundError`, killing the learner.

This is related to but not fixed by #4558: that PR normalizes images only in `to_lerobot_dataset()` (the write path). After it, checkpointing no longer crashes, but the in-memory offline buffer still trains on 0–255 images.

### Environment

```
- LeRobot version: 0.7.1
- Platform: Linux-6.8.0-149-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.35 (Ubuntu 22.04.5)
- Python: 3.12.12
- PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0
- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (32 GB), driver 580.178.04
- FFmpeg: 4.4.2
- Huggingface Hub: 1.33.0, Datasets: 4.8.5, NumPy: 2.2.6
- torchcodec: 0.11.1+cpu
```

Reproduced on `main` at `b0057180` (also `fe1c5459`), with [`lilkm/pick_cube_franka_panda_30`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/lilkm/pick_cube_franka_panda_30) (v3.0, both cameras stored as video). The dataset is public, so the repro below is self-contained.

### Root cause

1. `make_dataset()` loads camera features with `return_uint8=True` ([factory.py#L169](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/b00571809f7cab69abeee19744d8dd3c18977aa2/src/lerobot/datasets/factory.py#L169)). For video-backed cameras this returns uint8 0–255; image-backed (v2.x) cameras already return float [0, 1].
2. `_lerobotdataset_to_transitions()` copies the frames into the buffer unchanged ([buffer.py#L665](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/b00571809f7cab69abeee19744d8dd3c18977aa2/src/lerobot/rl/buffer.py#L665), [#L700](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/b00571809f7cab69abeee19744d8dd3c18977aa2/src/lerobot/rl/buffer.py#L700)).
3. `_initialize_storage()` allocates float32 tensors with `torch.empty()` ([buffer.py#L134-L150](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/b00571809f7cab69abeee19744d8dd3c18977aa2/src/lerobot/rl/buffer.py#L134-L150)), and `add()` copies the uint8 values into them ([buffer.py#L210](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/b00571809f7cab69abeee19744d8dd3c18977aa2/src/lerobot/rl/buffer.py#L210)). The buffer therefore holds float32 0–255.
4. The policy preprocessor expects [0, 1]: `normalization_mapping.VISUAL` is `MEAN_STD` and `dataset_stats` carries the ImageNet mean/std ([normalize_processor.py#L352-L365](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/b00571809f7cab69abeee19744d8dd3c18977aa2/src/lerobot/processor/normalize_processor.py#L352-L365)). The online buffer is correct because `VanillaObservationProcessorStep` divides by 255 ([observation_processor.py#L90](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/b00571809f7cab69abeee19744d8dd3c18977aa2/src/lerobot/processor/observation_processor.py#L90)); the offline buffer is not. `lerobot-train` already handles this in `_preprocess_dataset_batch()` ([lerobot_train.py#L175-L176](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/b00571809f7cab69abeee19744d8dd3c18977aa2/src/lerobot/scripts/lerobot_train.py#L175-L176)), but the RL path does not.
5. At checkpoint, `offline_replay_buffer.to_lerobot_dataset()` ([learner.py#L641-L648](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/b00571809f7cab69abeee19744d8dd3c18977aa2/src/lerobot/rl/learner.py#L641-L648)) passes those floats to `image_array_to_pil_image()`, which accepts float only in [0, 1] ([image_writer.py#L109-L113](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/b00571809f7cab69abeee19744d8dd3c18977aa2/src/lerobot/datasets/image_writer.py#L109-L113)). `write_image()` logs an error per frame but does not raise, so no PNGs exist. `save_episode()` then calls `compute_episode_stats()` → `sample_images()` → `load_image_as_numpy()`, which raises `FileNotFoundError` ([compute_stats.py#L255-L262](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/b00571809f7cab69abeee19744d8dd3c18977aa2/src/lerobot/datasets/compute_stats.py#L255-L262)) and terminates the learner.

### Reproduction

```python
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from lerobot.datasets.lerobot_dataset import LeRobotDataset
from lerobot.rl.buffer import ReplayBuffer

REPO_ID = "lilkm/pick_cube_franka_panda_30"
IMAGE_KEYS = ("observation.images.front", "observation.images.wrist")
STATE_KEYS = [*IMAGE_KEYS, "observation.state"]

# The learner gets this dataset from make_dataset(), which sets return_uint8=True.
ds = LeRobotDataset(REPO_ID, episodes=[0], return_uint8=True)
frame = ds[0]
for key in IMAGE_KEYS:
    t = frame[key]
    print(f"dataset[{key}]: dtype={t.dtype}, min={t.min().item()}, max={t.max().item()}")

buffer = ReplayBuffer.from_lerobot_dataset(
    ds,
    device="cpu",
    storage_device="cpu",
    state_keys=STATE_KEYS,
    capacity=len(ds),
    optimize_memory=True,
)
for key in IMAGE_KEYS:
    t = buffer.states[key][: len(ds)]
    print(f"buffer[{key}]: dtype={t.dtype}, min={t.min().item()}, max={t.max().item()}")

root = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "offline"
try:
    buffer.to_lerobot_dataset(REPO_ID, root=root)
except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
    print(f"to_lerobot_dataset raised {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
    print("PNG files written:", len(list(root.glob("images/**/*.png"))))
```

Output on `b0057180`:

```
len(ds) = 34
dataset[observation.images.front]: dtype=torch.uint8, min=5, max=255
dataset[observation.images.wrist]: dtype=torch.uint8, min=0, max=246
buffer[observation.images.front]: dtype=torch.float32, min=0.0, max=255.0
buffer[observation.images.wrist]: dtype=torch.float32, min=0.0, max=252.0

ERROR:lerobot.datasets.image_writer:Error writing image .../frame-000000.png: The image data type is float, which requires values in the range [0.0, 1.0]. However, the provided range is [5.0, 255.0]. Please adjust the range or provide a uint8 image with values in the range [0, 255].
...
to_lerobot_dataset raised FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '.../frame-000000.png'
PNG files written: 0
```

68 image-writer errors for 34 frames × 2 cameras. In a real run, the same happens at the first checkpoint; the learner exits with the `FileNotFoundError`, and `dataset_offline/` is left with `meta/info.json` and `meta/tasks.parquet` but `total_frames: 0`.

### Impact

- **Training:** with `online_ratio=0.5`, half of every batch has image inputs roughly 255× larger than the online half. MEAN_STD with ImageNet stats turns a [0, 1] image into roughly [-2, 2]; a [0, 255] image becomes roughly [-2, 1113]. It does not raise, so the corruption is silent.
- **Checkpointing:** the learner dies at the first checkpoint, and the resulting `dataset_offline` cannot be resumed from.

### Suggested fix

Normalize uint8 camera frames when ingesting the dataset, mirroring `lerobot_train.py`:

```python
for key in state_keys:
    val = current_sample[key]
    if key in dataset.meta.camera_keys and val.dtype == torch.uint8:
        val = val.to(torch.float32) / 255.0
    current_state[key] = val.unsqueeze(0)
```

Apply the same in the `next_state` loop. Notes:

- Image-backed (v2.x) datasets already return float [0, 1], so the dtype check makes this a no-op for them.
- Depth cameras are not uint8 (they decode as float in native units), so they are unaffected.
- The buffer already stores float32, so memory use does not change.

A regression test can live in `tests/utils/test_replay_buffer.py`: build a fake dataset returning uint8 camera tensors in [0, 255], assert the buffer's image entries are in [0, 1], and round-trip through `to_lerobot_dataset()` to verify the PNGs are written.

Alternative considered: load the offline dataset with `return_uint8=False`. `make_dataset()` hardcodes `True`, so this needs a factory change and would remove the uint8 fast path for `lerobot-train`; normalizing at ingestion is more targeted.

### Verified fix (local)

I implemented the fix above locally (normalize uint8 camera frames in `_lerobotdataset_to_transitions`, for both the current and next state) and added a regression test in `tests/utils/test_replay_buffer.py`. Results on the same episode:

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Buffer image dtype/range | float32, [0, 255] | float32, [0, 1] |
| `to_lerobot_dataset()` | 68 image-writer errors, then `FileNotFoundError` | succeeds: 34 frames / 1 episode |
| Reloaded image range | — | [0, 1] |
| Image-writer errors | 68 | 0 |

Normalized model inputs with the ImageNet mean/std from the RL config:

| Metric | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| mean | ≈ 430 | ≈ −0.29 |
| std | ≈ 240 | ≈ 1.0 |
| max | ≈ 1136 | ≈ 2.6 |

End-to-end smoke run (`save_freq=300`, `policy.online_steps=600`) on the same config:

- checkpoint 300 saved (`Checkpoint policy after step 300` → `Resume training`);
- `dataset_offline/`: 666 frames / 30 episodes, images `dtype: "image"`, data + episode metadata + stats complete;
- `dataset/` (online buffer): 400 frames / 4 episodes;
- 0 `Error writing image`, 0 tracebacks;
- reloaded `dataset_offline` images are in [0, 1];
- learner and actor shut down cleanly.

This confirms the input scale and checkpoint path. I have not run a long success-rate A/B; the 600-interaction run is only a stability check.

The patch is local; I can open a PR if this direction looks right.

### Related work

- #4558 — fixes the write path (`to_lerobot_dataset`) so checkpointing stops crashing; it does not fix the in-memory 0–255 training inputs. If #4558 merges first, the checkpoint-crash half of this report is fixed, but the offline training-input half remains.
- #4562 — makes RL checkpointing crash-safe and resumable; complementary.
- #3406 — introduced `return_uint8=True` in `make_dataset()`.

### Workaround

Until this is fixed, set `"dataset": null` in the RL config to train online-only (the offline buffer is only created when `cfg.dataset` is set), or apply the patch above. If a run has already died at a checkpoint, delete the run directory or at least `dataset_offline/`; resuming from a 0-frame offline dataset fails.

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing tickets to ensure this isn't a duplicate (closest: #4558, #4562; neither covers the training-input scale).
- [x] I am using the latest version of the `main` branch (`b0057180`).
- [x] I have verified this is not an environment-specific problem (public dataset, deterministic repro).
new_candidates.title: [Bug][RL] Offline replay buffer stores uint8 camera frames as float 0-255, corrupting offline training and checkpoint dumps

new_candidates.body:
`ros2_control_node` always uses a `MultiThreadedExecutor`. On a small arm64 robot, switching the executor roughly halves the node's idle CPU, so an opt-in option would help.

### Setup

- Raspberry Pi 5, ROS 2 Jazzy, ros2_control 4.48.1
- `update_rate: 100`, 2 hardware components, 4 controllers
- Robot idle

### Results

| Executor | CPU (% of one core) |
|---|---:|
| `MultiThreadedExecutor` (stock) | 31 |
| `SingleThreadedExecutor` | 25 |
| `EventsExecutor` (experimental) | 17 |

- Behaviour was the same in all three: controllers active, `joint_states` at 100 Hz, no overruns.
- Fewer threads don't help (2 threads ≈ 4 threads), so the cost is per-wakeup bookkeeping.

### Proposal

An option such as `multi_threaded | single_threaded | events`, defaulting to today's behaviour.

The executor is created before the CM node, so this probably has to be a command-line argument rather than a regular parameter.
new_candidates.title: ros2_control_node: allow choosing the executor to reduce idle CPU
